title: What we learned so far
caption: Long AI chats show the same effects as long calls, because the AI's attention span is its context window: a limited resource you manage actively.

two-kinds-of-evidence.description: the human pattern comes from lab word lists [1], the model pattern from retrieval tests on long inputs [2]; the match between them is an analogy, not a proof.

murdock-serial-position.title: Murdock, The serial position effect of free recall

liu-lost-in-the-middle.title: Liu et al., Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts

same-effects.title: Same effects
same-effects.script: Let's put it together. On the left, human attention: our memory follows the primacy and recency effects, so we recall the start, the end and the standout, and the middle blurs. On the right, AI attention shows the same shape in the context window.

the-window-is-the-span.title: The window is the span
the-window-is-the-span.script: The reason is that the AI's attention span is its context window, a limited space that fills with every message. That gives two lessons: important information and decisions get lost in the middle, and when the window is full, auto-compaction can drop details without telling you. Use the toggle on the window to switch between the plain view and the technical one.

manage-it.title: Manage it
manage-it.script: So learn to manage attention. For you it is optional, you will get by with a bad memory; for the AI it is mandatory. The rest of the episode is about what goes into that window, and what you do about it.
